<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 6:1">Ex. R. s. 6</cite>, end; Tanḥ. Vaëra 2 (prov.) <he>מן שטייא לית הנייא וכ׳</he> of acacias there is no profit except you cut them down, i.e. a wicked man can be converted by suffering only.—

<cite ref="Taanit 23b:7">Taan. 23ᵇ</cite> <he>מקרבא הַנְיָיתָהּ</he> Rashi (ed. <cite ref="E00680"><he>הנייתא</he></cite>) what good she does is a direct one (by giving bread); <he>ואנא … ולא מקרבא הנייתיה</he> (read: <he>הַנְיָיתִי</he>) but I give money, and what good I do is indirect; <cite ref="Ketubot 67b:13">Keth. 67ᵇ</cite> <he>ומקרבן אהנייתי</he> (read: <he>ומקרבא הַנְיָיתִי</he>, or <he>ומקרבן הֲנָיָיתַי</he>, pl.).—Y. B. Bath. V, 16ᵇ bot. <he>בנוי דה׳</he> (cmp. <cite ref="M02133"><he>מַעֲלֵי</he></cite>) good, worthy children.
